findings.namedBuyers: Priority sourcing contact: Raphael Gnininvi, Responsable Achats Indirects at Hublot since June 2026; profile states responsibility for Maison indirect purchasing and direct reporting to the CFO. Operational counterpart: Theepan Rasanayagam, Facility Manager, whose profile explicitly covers mobility, service-provider contracts and direct involvement in the new manufacture project. Emmanuelle Bouys, Events Senior Manager since July 2026, is relevant to inauguration/event planning. Seed contact Anouk Bradwell is Head of HR Administration & Systems since February 2024, not a verified relocation or accommodation buyer. None is publicly confirmed to control lodging contracts.
findings.futureEdition: No officially published exact start/end dates found for a relevant H3 activity within 2026-12-07–2028-06-30, assessed as of 2026-11-16. In the September 2026 CEO interview, Julien Tornare says: “you will hear a lot about it in 2027 because that will be the grand opening of that facility.” The 27 October 2026 project report says the building is already active, with progressive ramp-up through year-end, and: “Une inauguration sera alors agendée, sans qu’on ne connaisse encore la date précise.” 2027 is a stated opening year, not a confirmed need date; commissioning and ceremonial inauguration are different milestones. No subsequent dated edition identified.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: Nyon project geography supports a realistic Founex/La Côte corporate-lodging conversation. Best hypotheses are visiting technical teams, short-term assignees, installation/training support and event staff, subject to actual overnight need, transport, budget and length of stay. An internal production move does not itself prove employee residential relocation. Position YOTEL as practical lodging and optional small meetings/F&B, not a resort or an assumed luxury-client host. The supplied 20–120-room band is a sales capacity guideline, not published Hublot demand; no whole-house claim is justified.
findings.venueCommitments: Identified project site: Hublot H3 manufacture, La Vuarpillière / northern Nyon industrial area, Nyon, Vaud, Switzerland — within the Nyon/La Côte primary territory, not Geneva city or Lausanne. H3 lies east of the Nyon–Saint-Cergue–Morez railway. Hublot’s official registered headquarters is Chemin de la Vuarpillière 33, CH-1260 Nyon; this does not establish H3’s separate street number or an invitation-specific inauguration venue. No off-site event venue or hotel commitment verified.
findings.historicalRotation: No rotating event series established. The Hublot-issued 2015 release identifies the first Nyon plant opening in 2009 and the second building’s inauguration on 29 September 2015. H3 is a further Nyon campus expansion, not evidence of annual recurrence. A separate 2026 WatchTime reader trip visited Hublot and used Barcarolle in Prangins; it is not an H3 inauguration edition or a Hublot-owned housing programme.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown for H3 commissioning, relocation and inauguration: no public edition-specific housing bureau, host hotel, hotel block, open RFP or appointed lodging agency identified. No source was found that can be quoted as an H3 hotel-booking commitment. Separate historical evidence: WatchTime describes its 2026 multi-brand reader trip starting “im Hotel, dem schnucklig-entspannten Barcarolle in Prangins bei Nyon” and a Wednesday Hublot visit. Barcarolle is the only hotel named in that relevant visitor-trip evidence; this does not establish a Hublot corporate rate, incumbent H3 hotel, room block, or open inventory.
findings.organizationStructure: HUBLOT SA is a corporate luxury-watch manufacturer, not an association, PCO or DMC. Official legal notice identifies HUBLOT SA and its Nyon registered headquarters. The October 2026 report identifies it as part of LVMH since 2008. Hublot is the project owner/account; no external event organizer or housing intermediary was verified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: H3 itself includes meeting rooms and more than 500 sqm dedicated to visitor reception/experience, including a showroom of nearly 400 sqm; therefore external meeting-space demand cannot be presumed. Barcarolle, Prangins, is a documented historical base for an independently organized visitor trip, not a verified H3 incumbent. No H3 overflow, sell-out, hotel displacement or competing room-block evidence found. Inference: luxury-client hospitality may require a different hotel product; YOTEL’s operational-team proposition should be tested separately.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Raphael Gnininvi with a short corporate/project-stay capability brief and request a joint qualification conversation with Theepan Rasanayagam. Ask whether any non-local teams still require accommodation after 7 December 2026, their actual dates, lengths of stay, peak rooms, transport needs, incumbent hotels, travel-management route and approval process. Ask Emmanuelle Bouys separately whether the 2027 inauguration is scheduled and who manages guest/staff lodging. Use Anouk Bradwell as an HR referral only if employee relocation is confirmed. Offer negotiated terms only after need and access are established; do not hold rooms against an invented date.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Not currently sales-qualified as an open hotel requirement. The latest October report describes commissioning already underway, so construction/move-related stays may precede or overlap the research horizon. Neither exact residual work dates after 7 December 2026 nor overseas-team stays are verified. The proposed 2027 inauguration remains undated; sourcing openness and contract access are unknown, not closed or open by default.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: develop access to Hublot’s procurement/facilities teams now for any residual commissioning stays and future site visitors, training or inauguration support. The CEO describes the new facility as a hospitality tool, which supports asking about visitors but does not prove recurring overnight business. This is account development around a one-off expansion and possible later visitor demand, not a confirmed annual event-capture cycle.
